blocks.prompt: 10. A ball is thrown vertically upward with a velocity of 20 m/s. Find, the maximum height reached, and the time taken to return to the thrower's hand.
blocks.explanation:
Vertical motion with constant acceleration \(-g\) (upward positive), like Example 12.
Given: \(u = 20\) m/s. Find: the maximum height and the total time until the ball is back in the hand.
Plan: at the top \(v = 0\), so use \(2ax = v^2 - u^2\); back at the hand \(x = 0\), so use \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2\).
steps:
Given: \(u = 20\) m/s upward, \(a = -g = -9.8\ \text{m/s}^2\) (upward positive).
To find: the maximum height \(H\) and the time \(T\) to return to the hand.
Method: At the highest point \(v = 0\), and \(2ax = v^2 - u^2\) gives the height without needing the time. Back at the hand the displacement is zero, so \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2\) with \(x = 0\) gives \(T\).

Maximum height
\[2(-9.8)H = 0^2 - 20^2\]
\[-19.6H = -400\]
\[H = \dfrac{400}{19.6} = \dfrac{1000}{49}\]
\[H \approx 20.41\ \text{m}\]
Why: At the top the ball stops for an instant, so \(v = 0\).

Time to return to the hand
\[0 = 20T + \dfrac{1}{2}(-9.8)T^2\]
\[0 = T(20 - 4.9T)\]
\[T = 0\ \text{or}\ T = \dfrac{20}{4.9}\]
Why: Displacement is measured from the hand, so back at the hand \(x = 0\). Taking \(T\) common gives two roots.

Choose the correct root
\[T = \dfrac{200}{49} \approx 4.08\ \text{s}\]
Why: \(T = 0\) is the moment of throwing; the return to the hand is the other root.

Check
\[0 = 20 - 9.8t \Rightarrow t = \dfrac{20}{9.8}\]
\[t \approx 2.04\ \text{s},\quad 2t \approx 4.08\ \text{s}\ \checkmark\]
Why: \(v = u + at\) gives the time to the top (as in Example 12). Without air resistance the fall back takes as long as the rise, so the total is twice that. Example 12 also found the same height, about 20.4 m.
blocks.final_answer: Maximum height \(= \frac{1000}{49} \approx 20.41\) m; time to return to the hand \(= \frac{200}{49} \approx 4.08\) s.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: The book prints no answer for Exercise 7.1, so this answer is ours. It was checked independently with a computer algebra system and against an independent worked solution. The book's Example 12 has the same ball and finds the height and the time to the top; here we also need the time for the whole up-and-down trip.
